newsitem.title: UK: Tankers collide off French coast.
newsitem.headline: Tankers collide off French coast.

text.p: Two tankers collided in thick fog on Saturday in the North Sea and one was leaking unleaded petrol, British coast guards said.
No one was injured in the incident 30 miles northeast of Dover and neither ship was in danger of sinking, a coast guard spokesman said.
The tanker Bona Fulmar reported it had been in collision with the Mexican-registered chemical tanker Teoatl, Lloyd's casualty reporting service said.
"It occurred in very dense fog," Derek Smith of the Dover coast guard told Sky television. "The visibility was in the region of 300 yards (metres)."
He said the Bona Fulmar had lost about 3,000 cubic metres of unleaded petrol.
Smith said the collision occurred in French waters and French officials were coordinating the rescue with British assistance.
"Neither ship at the moment has anybody injured and neither ship appears in any danger of sinking," he added.
"We think the ships are waiting to be told where to go."
